notes: Current Marsannay parent production matrix. The red path deliberately keeps accessory white grapes out of the generic cellar-blend positive path; the rosé path admits only the two principal varieties until aggregate accessory-grape constraints can be represented exactly. Conditional white 4 g/L sugar allowance is conservatively omitted.

marsannay_masa_2020_cdc.scope: Published current modified AOC Marsannay cahier des charges: product colors, encépagement, vineyard management, maturity, yields, blending, analytical limits, oenological practices, élevage and market release.

specs.notes: White principal varieties are Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc. Pinot Gris is accessory in the vineyard (<=10% of planting) but may comprise up to 30% of the finished blend. The conditional 4 g/L fermentable-sugar ceiling is not promoted because its total-acidity predicate is not yet represented; the unconditional 3 g/L ceiling is used.

Conservative positive red path. Chardonnay, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris are legal accessories subject to a combined 15% blend ceiling, which the current per-variety constraint model cannot express safely; they therefore are not promoted as generic cellar-blend choices.

Positive rosé path contains only the two principal varieties, Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris. Chardonnay and Pinot Blanc accessories are omitted until their combined <=15% blend ceiling can be represented exactly. The specification sends rosé release to the general Code rural rule rather than the exact white/red 30 June calendar, so no exact Marsannay rosé release date is invented here.
